messages.content: what are the tools u know for booking flights

function.name: generate_image_tool
function.description: Generates an image based on the provided description and saves it with the specified file name. The image description should be detailed to ensure the resulting image matches the desired subject and surroundings; otherwise, these aspects will be chosen randomly. This function is not intended for generating images from textual data. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

desc.description: A single string that provides a detailed description of the desired image. For example, 'a sunset over the mountains with a lake in the foreground'.

file_name.description: The name of the file to which the generated image will be saved. It should include the file extension, such as 'image.png'.

function.name: tts_tool
function.description: Converts the provided text content to speech and saves the resulting audio to a file. This function is intended for voice narration and should be used accordingly. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

content.description: The text content that needs to be converted to speech.

speaker.description: The voice to be used for the text-to-speech conversion.

file_name.description: The name of the file to save the audio output without the extension. If left empty, a default name will be generated based on the content.

function.name: write_markdown_tool
function.description: Writes the provided content to a Markdown (.md) file on the disk. This function should be used when there is a need to persist text data in Markdown format as a result of a user action or a process that requires saving information in a structured text file. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

content.description: The Markdown formatted text content to be written to the file.

filename.description: The name of the file to which the Markdown content will be written. If not provided, a default filename will be used.

function.name: write_html_tool
function.description: Writes an HTML file to disk with the given content. Ensures HTML tags within the content are properly closed. This function should be used when there is a need to save HTML content to a file as part of a 'save' operation. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

content.description: The HTML content to be written to the file. Must contain valid HTML structure.

filename.description: The name of the file to which the HTML content will be written. If not provided, a default filename will be used.

function.name: search_web_tool
function.description: Executes a search query using the DuckDuckGo search engine and returns a specified number of search results from a given source. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

query.description: The search term or phrase to be queried.

num_results.description: The maximum number of search results to return. A positive integer.

source.description: The source from which the search results should be fetched.

function.name: get_url_content
function.description: Scrapes the specified URL for textual data and returns the content as a string. This function is useful for extracting information from web pages when a URL is provided. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The web address of the page to scrape. It should be a valid URL format, such as 'http://www.example.com'.

timeout.description: The maximum time in seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up, with a default value that allows for a reasonable amount of time for most web pages to load.

user_agent.description: The User-Agent string to be used for the HTTP request to simulate a particular browser, which is optional. Some websites may require this for access.

message.content:
Here’s a quick rundown of the main “tools” (websites, APIs, and platforms) you can use to book flights:

| Category | Tool / Service | What it offers | Typical use case |
|----------|----------------|----------------|------------------|
| **Online Travel Agencies (OTAs)** | **Expedia** | Aggregates flights, hotels, car rentals, packages. | General consumer bookings, multi‑service bundles. |
| | **Booking.com** | Primarily hotels but has a growing flight section. | Hotel‑centric travelers who want a flight add‑on. |
| | **Kayak** | Meta‑search engine that compares many OTAs. | Price comparison, flexible date searches. |
| | **Priceline** | Known for “Name Your Own Price” and Express Deals. | Last‑minute deals, budget travelers. |
| | **Orbitz** | Similar to Expedia, often bundled with loyalty points. | Frequent flyer programs tied to hotel stays. |
| | **Hotwire** | Offers “opaque” pricing for discounted seats. | Budget travelers willing to accept unknown seat assignments. |
| | **Travelocity** | Another OTA with a focus on package deals. | Family vacations, group bookings. |
| | **CheapOair** | Focuses on low‑fare tickets, often with promo codes. | Deal hunters, coupon users. |
| | **Skyscanner** | Meta‑search, strong price alerts, flexible dates. | Travelers looking for the cheapest possible date. |
| | **Google Flights** | Fast search, price graph, predictions. | Quick fare checks, itinerary planning. |
| | **Momondo** | Meta‑search, includes low‑cost carriers. | Comprehensive price comparison. |
| | **Trip.com** | Strong presence in Asia, integrates with local carriers. | International travelers, especially in Asia. |
| | **Opodo** | European OTA, often includes package deals. | European market, holiday packages. |
| | **Lastminute.com** | Focuses on last‑minute bookings. | Spontaneous travelers, last‑minute deals. |
| | **eDreams** | European OTA, often offers “price match” guarantees. | European travelers, price‑sensitive customers. |
| | **TUI** | Integrated travel agency, includes cruises. | Package holidays, cruise + flight combos. |
| | **Airbnb Experiences** | Not a flight booking tool per se, but sometimes bundles flights with experiences. | Experiential travelers. |
| | **Traveloka** | Southeast Asian OTA, strong mobile app. | Southeast Asian travelers, mobile‑first. |
| | **Ctrip (Trip.com)** | Chinese OTA, strong integration with Chinese carriers. | Chinese market, domestic flights in China. |
| | **MakeMyTrip** | Indian OTA, strong domestic coverage. | Indian travelers, domestic flights. |
| | **Cleartrip** | Indian OTA, focuses on simplicity. | Indian travelers, straightforward booking. |
| | **Yatra** | Indian OTA, strong customer support. | Indian travelers, customer service emphasis. |
| | **RedBus** | Bus booking, but sometimes bundles flights for long trips. | Long‑haul travelers combining bus & flight. |
| | **KAYAK** | Meta‑search, price alerts, flexible dates. | Price comparison, flexible itineraries. |
| | **Hopper** | Uses predictive analytics to suggest best booking times. | Travelers who want to wait for the best price. |
| | **Airfarewatchdog** | Alerts for specific routes, often includes hidden‑city fares. | Deal hunters, route‑specific alerts. |
| | **FlightAware** | Flight tracking, not booking, but useful for monitoring. | Tracking flight status, delays. |
| | **FlightStats** | Similar to FlightAware, provides real‑time flight data. | Monitoring, airline performance. |
| | **OpenSky Network** | Open‑data API for flight tracking. | Developers building flight‑tracking apps. |
| | **FlightRadar24** | Real‑time flight tracker, API available. | Flight tracking, aviation enthusiasts. |
| | **SITA** | Airline IT solutions, not a consumer tool. | Airline operations, B2B. |
| | **Amadeus** | Global distribution system (GDS), offers APIs for flight search. | Travel agencies, developers building booking engines. |
| | **Sabre** | GDS, offers APIs for flight inventory, booking. | Travel agencies, airlines. |
| | **Travelport** | GDS, offers APIs for flight, hotel, car. | Travel agencies, corporate travel. |
| | **IATA** | Industry standards, not a booking tool. | Industry compliance, data exchange. |
| | **SkyScanner API** | Meta‑search API for developers. | Building custom flight search widgets. |
| | **Google Flights API** | Not publicly available, but Google offers a Flights API via Google Cloud. | Developers building flight search features. |

* **Meta‑search engines** (Google Flights, Skyscanner, Kayak) pull data from multiple sources and give you a broad view of options.
* **GDS APIs** (Amadeus, Sabre, Travelport) are the backbone for travel agencies and corporate booking systems. They let you search inventory, hold seats, issue e‑tickets, and manage reservations programmatically.
* **Flight‑tracking APIs** (FlightAware, FlightRadar24, OpenSky) are useful if you need real‑time status, historical data, or analytics rather than booking itself.
* **Open data sets** (OpenFlights) are handy for research, building flight‑map visualizations, or training machine‑learning models.

If you’re building a product, pick the right mix: use a meta‑search or OTA for consumer‑facing price comparison, and hook into a GDS for actual ticket issuance. If you only need to show flight status or build a flight‑tracker, the tracking APIs are your go‑to.
